html:
The Weyanoke were an Algonquian-speaking people of the James River in Virginia, living on both banks downstream of today's Hopewell. They belonged to the paramount chiefdom of Powhatan when the English founded Jamestown in 1607.

English plantations soon spread onto their land, and in the 1600s the Weyanoke moved south, first to the Blackwater and Nottoway rivers and then into North Carolina, where they mixed with other Native peoples. Their neighbours on the James included the Appamattuck, Quiyoughcohannock and Chickahominy.
